content.comment_body: Hello. A customer reports an issue with a machine controlled by a [product_name]. The attached image shows a unit with article numbers [article_no] and [article_no]. The control uses only digital inputs and outputs, and is not networked—no Ethernet cable is connected, and no memory card is installed. No web page functionality is configured or active. How can this error be resolved, and what might cause it? Replacing the [product_name] is not possible due to lack of stock.

This message appears normally when accessing diagnostics for Ethernet using [product_name] [version_no], if no Ethernet cable is present. This happens whether or not a network connection is programmed. The message is visible in Main Menu > Diagnostics > Hardware > Ethernet, and is just informational—it does not affect the running program.
In the diagnostics menu, go to 'Toggle' to disable such errors with a red backlight. The 'Tools' menu in diagnostics also lets you view and clear the event log for the current session.

Thank you for your responses. I have a couple of questions: Shouldn't the situation change after a power cycle? (In this case, it does not.) What steps should I instruct the customer to follow to remove this message from the [product_name]? Would pressing the ESC button clear the message?

You can acknowledge such messages by pressing 'OK.' However, if no Ethernet cable is present, the message reappears. If the customer wants to suppress these diagnostics messages on the [product_name] display, they must disable this option in the diagnostics menu as previously suggested: Main Menu > Diagnostics > Toggle > Disable Toggle Event. Note that this disables all diagnostics messages.
The screenshot shows this message directly in the diagnostics Ethernet menu. The message reflects the actual status of the network cable—whether it is connected or not—and cannot be cleared.

Hello. I removed a [product_name] from a machine on our factory floor to test your suggestions and confirmed it has the same [article_no] as the problem device. I can access the error message from the diagnostic menu as described. I am unable to reproduce the error automatically after power cycling. The 'Toggle Event' only affects Menu > Diagnostics > Tools > View Event Log. I have not found a way to force the [product_name] to boot directly to the Network Error message. Is there something I am missing?

I also tested a [article_no] unit. Started with power on and Ethernet cable disconnected, but the [product_name] doesn't automatically enter the diagnostics menu. I am not aware of such behavior occurring automatically. PS: The screenshot is of a [article_no] ([version_no]).

Just commenting—no reply needed. Thank you for paying attention to detail; I incorrectly assumed the project office had given accurate information and should have checked. That saved me from making a poor decision. It does appear to be a [article_no], confirmed by the project. I have an older [version_no] to use as a temporary replacement, and the program is already adapted. Significant changes were needed since the older version. Thankfully, the [product_name] software provides reasons for upgrade/downgrade issues. Awaiting more feedback from the client.
If you are able to downgrade the program to an old [version_no], it likely means the program is fairly simple.
I'm still unsure why you want to change the [product_name]. The message does not affect program operation if the customer is not using communication features; it's only informational.

Hello [user_name], thanks for your interest. Feedback from the customer: The machine will not start; after booting, the error message is shown and ESC or OK does not clear it. Preparing an older [version_no] is a precaution. I believe the unit on site is faulty. [company_name] has no stock, and we don't have any available either; the older [version_no] is our best alternative if the device is damaged. I cannot reproduce the customer's exact situation; I can trigger the error message, but it does not persist through a power cycle. We will know more after a service visit. Best regards.

Update: The machine has resumed production. The error did not reappear when started today. The [product_name] was in STOP mode—I assisted the client in switching to admin mode and setting RUN. Unclear how it entered STOP while operator mode was active, but the important thing is production is ongoing.

I previously encountered a similar issue with a specific firmware version; after about 59 days of continuous operation, the [product_name] stopped due to a firmware error with an overflowing internal counter. The manufacturer did not officially disclose the problem; users had to discover it independently. You may have the same or a related issue. Regards.
I do not think your problem is related, as your [product_name] runs the current [version_no].

analysis.insight_summary: Users experienced a persistent 'network error' notification on [product_name] devices when no Ethernet cable is attached, visible in the diagnostics menu. This notice does not impact actual device operation, but its presence causes confusion about how to clear or suppress it. Users seek clearer error management, wish for better control over which notifications display by default, and are unsure about the function of the event log or the effect of power cycling and button presses on error persistence.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect irrelevant diagnostic notifications to be either suppressed or not persistent when networking features are inactive. They also desire straightforward instructions or simple methods to dismiss informational messages from the device's interface.
